old_note: *He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint. Do not the tears run down the widow's cheek? and is not her cry against him that causeth them to fall?* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 35:13-14 names THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the cry-of-the-bruised-heard-by-Yahuah (God) architecture: he-will-not-despise the supplication of the fatherless and the widow; the cry against the one who causes the tears reaches Yahuah (God). The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:20's bruised-reed-mercy substance: the wisdom-stream knew Yahuah (God) does not despise the bruised; the King at Matt 12:20 names the operative-disposition in his own ministry. The Pharisaic-system's plot at v.14 is precisely the act-causing-the-tears the wisdom-stream had named; the King's mercy-substance at v.20 is the operative-opposite-disposition.
new_note: *He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:14). *A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.* (Matthew 12:20). Sirach says Yahuah (God) does not despise the fatherless when they plead or the widow when she pours out her complaint. Matthew is quoting Isaiah about the servant who will not break a bruised reed or put out a smoking wick, and he says it of Yahusha (Jesus) in the same chapter where the Pharisees are plotting to destroy him. The ones who cause the tears and the one who hears them stand side by side. The widow's cry Sirach speaks of is heard by the same one who would not break a reed already bent.
writer_reason: Moved from 35:13 to 35:14: the old note quoted the fatherless-and-widow verse, which in the live text is 35:14, not 35:13 ('He will not accept any person against a poor man'). The old note's second sentence (the tears on the widow's cheek) is not in live 35:14 either; only 35:14 is quoted.

old_note: *And when we were carried away captives to Nineve, all my brethren, and those that were of my kindred, did eat of the bread of the Gentiles.* (Tobit 1:10). *For one believeth that he may eat all things: another, who is weak, eateth herbs* (Romans 14:2). The weak brother who *eateth herbs* is doing in Rome what Tobit did in the captivity — refusing the meat of the heathen table, whose slaughter and offering could not be trusted. The abstaining is a conscience guarding itself from defilement by association, not a verdict that the Torah's own clean food had changed.

old_note: *I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void; and the heavens, and they had no light. I beheld the mountains, and, lo, they trembled, and all the hills moved lightly. I beheld, and, lo, there was no man, and all the birds of the heavens were fled. I beheld, and, lo, the fruitful place was a wilderness, and all the cities thereof were broken down at the presence of Yahuah (LORD), and by his fierce anger.* (Jeremiah 4:23-26). Esdras is told that *the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain* (2 Esdras 7:30). Jeremiah was shown the like: the earth *without form, and void,* the heavens without light, and *lo, there was no man*. These are the words of the earth before the first day, when *the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep* (Genesis 1:2); the old silence is the earth returned to that first stillness, no man remaining, before *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her* (2 Esdras 7:32).
new_note: *And the world shall be turned into the old silence seven days, like as in the former judgments: so that no man shall remain.* (2 Esdras 7:30). *I beheld the earth, and, lo, it was without form, and void; and the heavens, and they had no light.* (Jeremiah 4:23). Esdras is told the world returns to the old silence for seven days, no man remaining. Jeremiah was shown the like: the earth *without form, and void,* the heavens without light, and, as he goes on, *lo, there was no man* (Jeremiah 4:25). These are the words of the earth before the first day, when *the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep* (Genesis 1:2); the old silence is the earth returned to that first stillness, no man remaining, before *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her* (2 Esdras 7:32).
